The test image shows a tomato leaf with a mottled, mosaic-like pattern — irregular patches of dark green and yellowish-green, no visible necrotic spots, no powdery coating, no lesions. The overall shape is intact but the coloration is uneven.

Top candidates: Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Verticillium_Wilt, Leaf_Mold.

Now I'll view one reference from each of my top 4 candidates.
CMV reference shows severe leaf distortion and curling — the test leaf is flat with no such distortion. Less likely CMV.
TSWV reference shows necrotic spots and bronzing — the test leaf has diffuse mottling without these spots. Less likely TSWV.
Verticillium Wilt reference shows marginal yellowing/necrosis — the test leaf has diffuse whole-leaf mottling, not marginal necrosis. Now checking Leaf_Mold.

Excellent match. The Leaf_Mold reference is nearly identical to the test image: same gray background, same single tomato leaf layout, same diffuse yellow-green mottling pattern with dark green interspersed — no distinct lesions, spots, or fungal growth visible on the upper surface. This is highly characteristic of Leaf Mold (upper surface chlorosis from *Passalora fulva*).

All 4 reference views used across 4 different classes. Leaf_Mold is the clear match.
